blocks.text: **The problem.** Letters are encoded as numbers: `A = 1`, `B = 2`, …, `Z = 26`. Given a string of digits `s`, return the **number of ways to decode it**. A piece like `06` is not valid — no letter is encoded with a leading zero.

blocks.alt: s = 226. ways[i] counts the decodings of the first i digits. ways[0] = 1 (the empty prefix) and ways[1] = 1 (just 2). For ways[2], the last digit 2 alone gives ways[1] = 1, and the pair 22 gives ways[0] = 1: 2 ways. For ways[3], 6 alone gives ways[2] = 2, and 26 gives ways[1] = 1: 3 ways — BZ, VF and BBF.

elements.text: the last letter used one digit (1-9) or two digits (10-26)

blocks.code:
s = "12"   ->  2   ("AB" from 1 2, "L" from 12)
s = "226"  ->  3   ("BZ", "VF", "BBF")
s = "06"   ->  0   (a leading zero can't be decoded)

blocks.text: The idea: the last letter used one or two digits

Let `ways[i]` be the number of decodings of the first `i` digits. The last letter of a decoding used either **one digit** — valid if `s[i−1]` isn't `0` — leaving `ways[i−1]` decodings for the rest, or **two digits** — valid if `s[i−2..i−1]` is between 10 and 26 — leaving `ways[i−2]`. Add the valid cases. `ways[0] = 1`: the empty string has one (empty) decoding. Zeros are the whole difficulty: `0` can only appear as part of `10` or `20`.
**Time O(n), space O(n).** This version reads the string **forwards from i**, so its table would fill right to left — either direction works.

blocks.caption: Each prefix adds the one-digit and the two-digit ways to finish it.

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(n)** — or O(1) with two variables, exactly as in Climbing Stairs (which this is, with rules about which steps are allowed).

blocks.alt: Memoized recursion: O(n) time, O(n) space. Table over prefixes: O(n) time, O(n) space.

items: **Zeros that pair** — `"10"`, `"2101"`: the 0 must join the digit before it.
**Decode Ways II** — `*` stands for any digit 1–9: the same recurrence with counts per case, modulo 10⁹ + 7.
**Climbing Stairs** — the same shape without the digit rules.
**Word Break** — the last piece is any dictionary word instead of one or two digits (Pattern 4).
